text: Chapter one's loop doesn't end at made a change. It ends at verify -- measuring again and confirming the exact bottleneck actually moved, without quietly breaking something else. This lesson runs that step for real against the new IX_Orders_CustomerID_OrderDate index.

Verification only means something if it's measuring the same thing Lesson 48 measured. Running dbo dot usp_CustomerOrderHistory for CustomerID forty-eight thousand two-thirteen again, with SET STATISTICS IO, TIME ON: before, about twenty-eight thousand milliseconds elapsed, about a hundred eighteen thousand logical reads, Key Lookup executed eighteen thousand four hundred times. After, about eighty-five milliseconds elapsed, about three hundred fifty logical reads, no Key Lookup operator in the plan at all -- just a single Index Seek against the new index that returns already-sorted, fully-covered rows. More than a three-hundred-x drop on both duration and logical reads.

Chapter one warned against declaring victory off a single number. Checking sys dot dm_os_wait_stats, or Query Store's wait-stats breakdown for this query, during the next ten AM to two PM window shows PAGEIOLATCH_SH waits attributable to this query have dropped to essentially nothing -- consistent with the plan no longer scattering eighteen thousand four hundred random-page reads through the buffer pool per execution. Plan, metrics, and waits all agree.

Lesson 47's guide called out the classic trap: a change that helps reads while quietly hurting writes. dbo dot Orders gets thousands of new rows a day, and every nonclustered index adds a small maintenance cost to every INSERT. But Lesson 49 already dropped the redundant IX_Orders_CustomerID -- so the table maintains the same number of nonclustered indexes it did before, just one wider one instead of one narrow one. Comparing sys dot dm_db_index_usage_stats write counts, and checking Query Store for newly-regressed INSERT plans, confirms no measurable write-side regression.

The specific operator named in diagnosis is gone from the plan. The specific metrics baselined in diagnosis dropped by orders of magnitude, for the same input. The specific wait type identified in diagnosis dropped correspondingly. And the specific risk called out up front was checked and ruled out. Four independent confirmations -- not one lucky-looking number.
